author: claude
desc: Measure the real limit on an m1n1-decoded xz initramfs. MEASURED SO FAR: expanded initramfs of 13.1, 50.8, 60.5 and 97.3 MiB all decode and boot; 278.9 MiB fails with m1n1 printing 'XZ decode failed', no 'FDT: initrd at' line, and the kernel therefore booting with an empty rootfs (rdinit=/sbin/init -> -2, then 'VFS: Cannot open root device' and reboot). The true limit lies in (97.3, 278.9] MiB. RULED OUT already, by inspection not assumption: XZ block-header size metadata (byte 13 flags are 0x0000 on every member, working and failing alike, so minilzlib's documented 'size metadata indicator' restriction is not it) and dictionary/filter differences (xz -lvv reports identical 1 stream / 1 block / CRC32 / 1 filter / 65 MiB for all). SUSPECT: m1n1's src/payload.c decodes into heapblock_alloc_aligned(0, KERNEL_ALIGN) — the uncommitted heap top — with dest_len = 1<<30, and heapblock_alloc_aligned performs NO bound check. TASK: bisect with intermediate rootfs sizes (try 128, 160, 192, 224 MiB expanded) OR, cheaper and offline first, build a host harness around m1n1's src/minilzlib (portable C, needs only stddef/stdint/stdbool/assert plus one ../utils.h include) and call XzDecode on the real members to find the threshold with no rig time. Then either fix m1n1's decompress path or set the verifier guard to the measured value. The verifier guard is currently 128 MiB — above every proven-good size, below the known-bad one — and MUST NOT be raised without a live boot proving the larger size decodes. Evidence: done/2026-07-26-t6040-initramfs-decode-limit.md.
